A 25-year-old G2P3 female presents to the clinic with complaints of low back pain. She is one week
postpartum following an uncomplicated vaginal delivery of twins. The pain began four days ago after
returning home from the hospital. On examination, the seated flexion test is positive on the right. When
the patient is prone and moves onto her elbows, the bilateral sacral sulci and inferior lateral angles
(ILAs) appear symmetrical. In the anatomic position, the right sacral sulcus is deep, and the left ILA is
inferior. What is the most likely diagnosis for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Right unilateral sacral
flexion (B) Bilateral sacral extension (C) Sacral base posterior (D) Left on left sacral torsion (E) Sacral
base anterior (F) Right on right sacral torsion (G) Bilateral sacral flexion (H) Left on right sacral torsion
(I) Left unilateral sacral extension (J) Right on left sacral torsion
 A. Bilateral sacral flexion
B. Left on left sacral torsion
C. Sacral base anterior
D. Left unilateral sacral extension
E. Left on right sacral torsion
F. Right on right sacral torsion
G. Bilateral sacral extension
H. Right on left sacral torsion
I. Right unilateral sacral flexion
J. Sacral base posterior
